title: APS Journal Fit Assessment
description: Structured output contract for a single manuscript-to-journal fit assessment. Use when a caller wants machine-readable output instead of the prose format in each journal skill. Field meanings follow the skills; this schema does not relax any of their rules.

criterion_claimed.description: For journals with enumerated acceptance criteria (PRL, PRX, PRX Quantum, PRX Energy, PRX Intelligence): the specific criterion claimed, quoted or named, with justification.

ai_ml_decomposition.description: Required when the manuscript uses AI/ML. Mirrors the five-way decomposition in the PRX Intelligence and PRB skills.

staleness_flag.description: Set when the journal skill's last_verified exceeds its refresh_interval_days.

mathematical_presentation.description: Required for theoretical, computational, or equation-driven manuscripts. Mirrors the Mathematical presentation profile in each journal skill and the framework in aps-mathematical-presentation. Omit, or set applicable=false, when the contribution is not equation-driven — manufacturing mathematical criticism of a measurement or characterization paper is a failure mode.

central_mathematical_object.description: The equation, relation, or model expressing the central contribution — or a note that the manuscript possesses one but never writes it down.

density_mismatch.description: Placement information, not a defect: a density wrong for this journal is often right for a neighbor.

essential_equations_fit_format.description: False means the article type or journal should change — never that an essential equation should be cut.

equation_audit.description: Displayed equations with no identifiable purpose, or algebra that does not advance the argument.

interpretation_gaps.description: Important equations presented without physical reading; undefined symbols; approximations without a validity regime.

presentation.description: Format and presentation assessment. Mirrors the Presentation profile in each journal skill and aps-format-and-presentation. Every statement should be attributable to one of the bindingness labels.

article_type_length_limit.description: The journal's verified limit for this type, or 'No explicit limit stated in official sources'. Never estimated.

figure_strategy.description: Derived from the scientific narrative. Never a target number, and never asserted as a journal requirement — no APS journal examined states a figure limit.

figure_audit.description: Figures proving nothing new, doing two jobs, or duplicating another; central claims lacking a figure.

compression_opportunities.description: Related figures combinable into a unified multi-panel figure. Never unrelated results merged to reduce a count.

misplaced_content.description: Content essential to understanding or evaluating the central claim that sits in Supplemental Material — a defect, since APS defines SM as non-essential material.

joint_submission_recommended.description: True when the work is both pivotal and genuinely needs length; APS permits a Letter plus a longer article elsewhere.

references.description: Reference-list audit. Mirrors aps-reference-format. Mechanics apply portfolio-wide; only journal-specific exception on record is PRL's titles-in-references convention.

completeness.description: Any citation in main text, captions, or Supplemental Material missing from the list; any listed item never cited.

author_count_handling_correct.description: All authors listed up to ten; up to twenty plus et al. beyond that.

urls_in_body_text.description: Should be false — URLs belong in the reference list, not the body.

eprints_used_as_primary_reference.description: Should be false where a peer-reviewed version exists.

currency.description: Whether the list is up to date as of the current submission or revision.

representativeness.description: Whether competing groups, regions, and institutions look represented — an APS-stated expectation, not only a formatting concern.

$comment: There is deliberately no field for predicted acceptance, acceptance probability, or editorial outcome. The skills forbid such predictions; the schema does not provide a place to record one. Likewise there is no field for equation count or a mathematical-quality score: density and hierarchy are fit and clarity dimensions, and mathematical complexity is never recorded as significance. Presentation advice carries a second labeling axis — REQUIREMENT / CONVENTION / STRATEGY — recorded in presentation.label_audit; a REQUIREMENT without a source_url is invalid. There is likewise no numeric self-citation threshold field: APS states the principle (representativeness, no inflation), not a percentage, and the schema does not invent one.
